newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian president wants stable government.
newsitem.headline: Indian president wants stable government.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma on Sunday asked the Congress party to prove that a new centre-left government would be more stable than its predecessor which fell in 10 months, party leaders said.
The president, charged under the constitution with naming the prime minister, sought the assurances from Congress in a meeting with party president Sitaram Kesri, Congress members said.

"President Sharma has asked the Congress party to show reliable proof that the new government will not be an unstable one," a senior Congress official told Reuters after a meeting of the party's policy-making Congress Working Committee.
Congress officials said the president had asked that Congress and the United Front establish a mechanism for ensuring that the next government is a stable one.

Earlier on Sunday, United Front leaders met Sharma to stake a claim to form a new centre-left government after electing Inder Kumar Gujral as their new leader. But Sharma was waiting for assurances the next government would be more stable before naming Gujral prime minister, politicians said.

The United Front's decision-making Steering Committee was scheduled to meet at 4 p.m. (1030 GMT) to take up the question of establishing more stable ties with Congress, which provoked the downfall of caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government by withdrawing its vital support.
